title: Best Android App Developers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire an Android app developer: what the project should include, device testing, Play Store publishing, price factors and red flags.
intro: Android runs on a huge range of phones and tablets, from budget devices to flagships, which makes it a large market but also a demanding one to build for. An Android developer builds, tests and publishes your app on Google Play. Projects go wrong when the app is only tested on one phone, the Play Store account belongs to the developer, or privacy and permission rules are ignored. This guide helps you launch smoothly.

faq.q: Should I build Android only, or Android and iPhone together?
faq.a: It depends on your users. Cross-platform frameworks can build both from one codebase; a native Android app may suit apps that need deep device features. Ask the developer about the trade-offs for your case.
A range: at least one older, lower-powered phone, a recent phone, and different screen sizes. Your analytics or target market tells you which matter most.

faq.q: Who owns the Google Play account?
faq.a: You. Create the developer account in your own or your company's name and add the developer as a user.
Access to things like location, camera or contacts. Ask for only the permissions the app truly needs, and explain them to users. Google Play reviews sensitive permissions carefully.
Store listing, screenshots, privacy information, content rating and review. Plan time for it before your launch date.
